newsitem.title: USA: Rite-Aid agrees with yr EPS estimate $2.15.
newsitem.headline: Rite-Aid agrees with yr EPS estimate $2.15.

text.p: Rite-Aid Corp Chairman Martin Grass told Reuters he was comfortable with estimates that the firm would earn $2.15 a share for fiscal 1997, ending next month.
Grass also said at an Emerald Asset Management investment forum that the firm expected annual earnings gains of 15 pct for the next three years.
He said Rite-Aid expected revenues of slightly more than $11 billion for fiscal 1998.
In fiscal 1996 Rite-Aid reported earnings of $1.90 a share on revenues of $5.4 billion.
Grass told the forum that Rite-Aid would open about 150 new stores in fiscal 1998 and would replace about 250 existing stores with new, larger stores.
About 35 of the new-store openings will come in the western United States, where Rite-Aid recently acquired 1,000 stores in buying Thrifty Payless Inc.
About 150 new stores will be opened in fiscal 1999, including 50 to 60 in the west. He said 175 to 200 stores would be opened in the following year, about equally divided between east and west.
Drug store industry consolidation will continue, he said, driven by continued growth in third-party payment of pharmaceutical costs.
Other growth areas for Rite-Aid include cosmetics, convenience foods, and photo processing, Grass said.
